slides.title: The retail AI windfall illusion
slides.card_text: Retail investors view the targeted October listing on Nasdaq as early-stage upside. In reality, private VCs use public markets to offload massive capital expenditure liabilities before inevitable 3.8x margin compression hits enterprise compute models.

slides.title: Offloading massive CapEx liabilities
slides.card_text: Cloud hyperscalers lock in paper multiples while passing infrastructure debt to public equity holders. Buying at listing converts hyper-growth valuation expectations into paying off billions in compute debt while early backers exit at peak enterprise pricing.

slides.title: The institutional exit liquidity engine
slides.card_text: Late-stage venture funds face severe internal rate of return hurdles. Public retail order flow provides necessary volume for insiders to distribute positions before the post-listing 180-day lockup expiry triggers structural dilution and aggressive selling pressure.

slides.title: Quantifying the valuation decay rate
slides.card_text: Mega-cap tech listings entering with negative free cash flow historically experience a 42% valuation haircut over 12 months as server depreciation and GPU replenishment costs erode gross margins below sustainable 15% enterprise thresholds.

slides.title: The 180-day execution rule
slides.card_text: Never allocate capital to mega-cap hype listings or correlated proxy baskets during the initial 180-day lock-in period. Wait until audited post-listing free cash flow and unit economics validate long-term operational sustainability.

slides.title: The 3-point pre-listing audit
slides.card_text: Before allocating capital, verify: 1) Positive free cash flow trajectory net of compute costs; 2) Less than 20% insider distribution at lockup expiry; and 3) Sustainable enterprise customer retention above 120% net expansion.
